chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever is involved in adjudication, let him not judge while he is angry.

key_terms.الْقَضَاء: Adjudication, judicial ruling, the office of judge (qadi)
key_terms.غَضْبَان: Angry, in a state of anger or rage — a condition that invalidates judicial fitness

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a judge to give a ruling while angry in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports this prophetic ruling that a judge must not issue verdicts while in a state of anger. This teaching reflects the Islamic principle that sound judgment requires a composed and clear-minded state, since anger clouds reason and may lead to injustice. This hadith was particularly relevant to the community of early Islamic jurists and judges who were establishing standards for judicial conduct.
